findings.title: Warn message interpolates the module object instead of the app type string
findings.body: Line 18: `console.warn(`payment App service of type ${paymentApp} is not implemented`);` — `paymentApp` is now the awaited module namespace (an object), so the log will render the app type as `[object Module]` instead of the actual dirName. This makes the warning useless for debugging which payment app is misconfigured. Use `paymentAppCredentials?.app?.dirName` in the message. Same issue in `packages/lib/payment/handlePayment.ts` line 28 and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` line 969.

findings.title: Warn message interpolates the module object instead of the app type string
findings.body: Line 28: `console.warn(`payment App service of type ${paymentApp} is not implemented`);` — `paymentApp` is the awaited module namespace object, so the message prints `[object Module]` rather than the payment app's dirName. This obscures which app failed. Interpolate `paymentAppCredentials?.app?.dirName` instead. Same defect in `packages/lib/payment/deletePayment.ts` line 18, `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts` line 591, and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` line 969.

findings.title: Warn message interpolates the module object instead of the app type string
findings.body: Line 969: `console.warn(`payment App service of type ${paymentApp} is not implemented`);` — after `const paymentApp = await appStore[...]`, `paymentApp` is the resolved module namespace object, so the warning prints `[object Module]` instead of the payment app's dirName, making it impossible to tell which app is unimplemented. Use `paymentAppCredential?.app?.dirName` in the template string.

findings.title: getCalendar result awaited but deleteEvent call not awaited inside updateAllCalendarEvents merge path
findings.body: In `updateAllCalendarEvents`, the merge path (when `newBookingId` is set) does `const calendar = await getCalendar(calendarCredential);` at line 488 followed by `await calendar?.deleteEvent(oldCalendarEvent.uid, event, oldCalendarEvent.externalCalendarId);` at line 489. The `await` on line 489 is present, so this specific call is fine. However, note that `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` — if `calendar` is `null` (e.g. unknown credential type or failed dynamic import), the expression short-circuits to `undefined` and `await undefined` resolves immediately, silently skipping the deletion of the old calendar event during a booking merge. There is no log or error when the old event fails to be deleted, so a merge can leave an orphaned event on the external calendar. Consider logging when `calendar` is null in this path.

findings.title: No tests cover the async appStore contract; consumers that forget to await will fail silently at runtime
findings.body: The PR converts every `appStore` entry from an eagerly-imported module namespace into a dynamic-import `Promise`. This is a breaking change to the shape of the default export, and the safety of the migration depends entirely on every call site remembering to `await` the indexed value before accessing `.lib` / `.config`. The PR updates the known call sites, but there is no test that exercises `appStore` access patterns (e.g. a unit test asserting `await appStore.googlecalendar` exposes `lib.CalendarService`, or a type-level test that `appStore` values are promises). A consumer that does `const app = appStore[x]; if ("lib" in app)` without `await` will silently skip the integration (the `"lib" in app` check on a Promise is false) with no error. Recommend adding a test that iterates all appStore entries, awaits them, and asserts each resolves to a module with the expected shape, plus a type test ensuring consumers must await.
